title: paged KV cache: allocator reuse + locality-aware pinning + TTL improvements
author: Liam Chen
commits: Feature: add reuse pool to block_allocator with lock-free freelist
Feature: locality-aware pinning heuristics in block_manager
Feature: TTL-based eviction path for paged KV cache
Perf: batch hot-path to avoid per-allocation mutex wakeups
Test: new unit + integration tests for reuse & pinning
Bench: microbench harness and CI bench job updates
Docs: add rollout notes and compatibility guidance
description:
Context & motivation: The paged KV cache has historically seen allocation churn under continuous-batching workloads and long-running chat sessions. This churn causes mutex contention and repeated device-host copies when blocks are recycled, leading to p99 latency spikes and reduced throughput under high-concurrency inference workloads. Previous PRs introduced basic reuse/pinning but left locality and TTL behavior suboptimal.

What this PR does: Implements a set of coordinated improvements to the paged KV cache block manager and allocator to reduce allocation churn and improve locality for hot KV entries. Changes include: 1) a reuse pool in the block allocator that keeps recently freed blocks warm and avoids expensive zeroing/copying on reallocation, implemented as a bounded lock-free freelist; 2) locality-aware pinning logic in the block manager that prefers reusing blocks on the same GPU / memory bank when available; 3) a TTL-driven lazy-eviction path that evicts cold pages in the background to avoid eviction storms during capacity pressure; 4) batching of hot-path allocation bookkeeping to reduce mutex wakeups; and 5) new metrics and bench harness to verify gains.

Implementation notes: The allocator exposes a reuse pool API surface that is backwards-compatible with the previous allocator interface. The reuse pool is bounded and sized via runtime config with sane defaults derived from observed working set sizes in production (see docs/changes). Locality-aware pinning uses per-device LRU buckets and prefers local-device blocks when reassigning pages, falling back to inter-device placement only when necessary. TTL eviction runs on a background worker and uses adaptive rate-limiting to avoid IO spikes. Care was taken to avoid adding blocking syscalls on the inference hot-path; most work is done by lock-free structures or background tasks.

Compatibility and rollout: No public API changes. Defaults are conservative: reuse pool enabled with small default size; locality pinning enabled. Feature gates added so SRE can disable/rollback quickly. This was rolled out to canary traffic for Dedicated and Hosted regions over a 48-hour window before full merge.

Testing & CI: Added unit tests for allocator edge-cases and integration tests for cross-device reuse/pinning semantics. Bench harness exercises continuous-batching workloads similar to real production traces. CI initially showed a flaky bench run (timeout on bench VM); fixed by reducing unnecessary logging and adding a retry in the bench job. Final CI: build + unit tests + bench + lint all passed.

Performance: Microbench and canary traffic show consistent improvements: ~18% end-to-end throughput uplift on batched generation workloads, p99 latency reduced by ~12% under loaded conditions, and allocation-related CPU contention down ~45% in our profiler. Memory overhead is nominal (reuse pool + per-device metadata), and evictions are smoother with TTL-enabled background eviction.

Follow-ups: 1) Expose reuse pool sizing recommendations in Redwood Console (ENG-5901); 2) Consider hardware-topology aware placement beyond device-level (NUMA, PCIe locality); 3) Add per-customer hints for pinning sensitivity.
review_comments: Ava Martinez: This looks good overall. Two requests: 1) can you add a metric for reuse-pool hit rate, and 2) clarify the behavior when the reuse pool is full?

Liam Chen (author): Added reuse_pool_hit_rate and documented that when the pool is full we fall back to standard allocator which will either zero the block or reuse a cold block depending on config. Updated metrics and docs.
Priya Nair: Locality-aware pinning is promising — did you validate cross-device fallback won't create device imbalance? The bench results are encouraging but I'd like a stress test across devices.

Liam Chen (author): Added an integration stress test exercising multi-device imbalance scenarios; the pinning heuristics include a skew threshold to force fallback and avoid full saturation of a single device.
Eliot Brooks: One nit: TTL eviction worker should be configurable with minimum interval to avoid busy loops. Also please add a short note in rollout docs about rollback steps.

Liam Chen (author): TTL worker interval made configurable and default set to 5s with exponential backoff under load. Rollout doc updated with explicit rollback steps (feature gate off + repeatable clear).
benchmarks: bench/kv_block_reuse_bench: continuous-batching workload: throughput +18% (p50), p99 latency -12%
canary/hosted-us-west: sustained 24h: allocation CPU contention -45%, swap/copy events reduced ~60%
dedicated/canary-eu: 12h: stable under 3x baseline QPS without p99 regressions
release_notes: Paged KV cache: improved block allocator reuse, locality-aware pinning, and TTL-driven eviction. Reduces allocation churn and improves batching throughput and latency. Opt-out via feature gate if needed.
